entry.title: React at 1000Hz: Optimizing Real-Time Performance
entry.summary:
The Performance Wall: Why React Isn't a Data Buffer
If you’ve ever built a real-time application—a trading dashboard, a crypto ticker, or a live sensor monitor—you’ve likely hit the "React Performance Wall." You pipe your WebSocket messages directly into useState, and suddenly, your browser becomes a stuttering, unresponsive mess. The culprit is simple but often misunderstood: React is a UI library, not a data buffer. When you treat React state as the ultimate source of truth for every single byte of incoming data, you are essentially asking React to trigger a reconciliation cycle for every packet.
